parts.what: the stream survives every change without reconnecting
parts.seen: one peer connection throughout, "connected" after every change (a: connected, l: connected, b: connected, e: connected, c: connected, d: connected, h: connected). From the ask to the first decoded frame at the new size: (b) 287 ms, (c) 288 ms, (d) 294 ms

parts.what: the panel's own keys do what they say
parts.seen:
yes: [ SETTINGS ] opens the panel
      yes: the panel says what the PC is really sending
      yes: pressing [ 16:9 ] and [ 1080 ] changed the picture (decoded 1920x1080)
      yes: the [ 16:9 ] key shows as pressed
      yes: FAST is in use by default (drawing "fast"); the browser gave its canvas the skip-the-queue kind
      yes: FAST, OFF: the canvas holds 1920x1080, the picture is 1920x1080 on the page, 58 frames were drawn while 58 were decoded, 19% of the sampled points are lit, and it is on average 0.00 levels (of 255) from the plain frame (most 0)
      yes: FAST, SMOOTH: the canvas holds 1920x1080, the picture is 1280x720 on the page, 56 frames were drawn while 56 were decoded, 100% of the sampled points are lit, and it is on average 0.00 levels (of 255) from the plain frame (most 0)
      yes: FAST, SHARP: the canvas holds 1920x1080, the picture is 1280x720 on the page, 54 frames were drawn while 54 were decoded, 19% of the sampled points are lit, and it is on average 0.00 levels (of 255) from the plain frame (most 0); hard squares: true
      yes: FAST, SHARPENED: the canvas holds 1280x720, the picture is 1280x720 on the page, 57 frames were drawn while 57 were decoded, 100% of the sampled points are lit, and it is on average 1.17 levels (of 255) from the plain frame (most 65)
      yes: [ NORMAL ] hands the picture to the browser's own player (the FAST canvas is gone)
      yes: NORMAL, OFF shows the picture at its real size (1920x1080 drawn 1920x1080)
      yes: NORMAL, SHARP draws in hard squares (image-rendering: pixelated)
      yes: NORMAL, SMOOTH fits the window (1280x720)
      yes: NORMAL, SHARPENED draws a 1280x720 canvas, 34 frames so far, 100% of the sampled points lit, and on average 1.17 levels (of 255) away from the plain picture (most 65)
      yes: [ FAST ] takes it back
      yes: [ NUMBERS ] takes the corner readout away
      yes: and puts it back
      yes: the READOUT shows the stream
      yes: [ FULLSCREEN ] took the page fullscreen
      yes: the choices are remembered on this device ({"match":false,"shape":"16:9","lines":1080,"fps":60,"bitrateKbps":20000,"drawing":"fast","upscaling":"smooth","numbers":true,"mouse":"pointer"})
      yes: Esc closes the panel

parts.what: on a new visit the remembered settings are sent to the PC again
parts.seen: after a reload the PC was asked for 16:9 at 1080 lines; the browser decoded 1920x1080

parts.what: a match starting mid-stream caps it, and what was asked for comes back when the match ends
parts.seen: before: 2560x1440 at 30000 kbit/s; match "started": 1920x1080 at 12000 kbit/s, cap "LEAGUE MATCH", seen by the page 2095 ms later; match "ended": 2560x1440 at 30000 kbit/s, seen 3004 ms later; connection connected, 1 made (the engine looks for the game once a second and the page reads the PC's settings every 3 s, so a few seconds is expected)

parts.what: where FAST cannot run the page says so and draws NORMAL; the address can ask for either
parts.seen:
yes: opened with "?fast=refused&hold=1": 7 frames decoded, drawn NORMAL, and the panel says "FAST cannot run here (this browser was told to refuse it, as a test), so the picture is drawn NORMAL instead."
      yes: opened with "?drawing=normal&hold=1": 7 frames decoded, drawn NORMAL, and the panel says "This page's address asks for NORMAL (drawing=normal), so that is used whatever is chosen here."
      yes: opened with "?drawing=fast&hold=1": 7 frames decoded, drawn FAST, and the panel says "This page's address asks for FAST (drawing=fast), so that is used whatever is chosen here."

parts.what: FRAMES A SECOND on AUTO follows the viewer's screen, up to the PC's own
parts.seen:
yes: left alone, the page measured its own screen at 180 frames a second and asked for AUTO with it (the PC was asked for "auto" at 180); the PC is sending up to 180
      yes: a pretended 144 Hz viewer on AUTO: the PC (whose own screen shows 180) sends up to 144 (wanted 144)
      yes: a pretended 240 Hz viewer on AUTO: the PC (whose own screen shows 180) sends up to 180 (wanted 180)
      yes: the panel shows [ AUTO ] pressed and says: "AUTO follows this screen. This screen shows 180 frames a second (measured here). The PC sends that many when its own screen and its limits allow."
